mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz CLA 220d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a CLA 220d typically costs between £1,200 and £4,200 depending on the engine code and condition. Used N47D20C units start from £1,200-£2,200, reconditioned from £2,200-£3,200, and fully rebuilt OM654 engines from £2,800-£4,200. Labour for supply & fit adds £450-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a CLA 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: On N47D20C-equipped CLA 220d models (C117, 2015-2019), the most common symptom is a rattling or metallic noise from the rear of the engine, particularly at 2,500-3,000 rpm. Other signs include loss of power, rough idle, engine misfires, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately - ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Does the CLA 220d have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the engine and generation. The N47D20C (CLA 220d, C117, 2015-2019) uses a timing chain positioned at the rear of the engine - a design that makes replacement labour-intensive. The OM654.920 (CLA 220d, C118, 2019-present) also uses a timing chain, which is generally more robust but can suffer from tensioner wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz CLA 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A C117 CLA 220d is typically worth £4,000-£8,000 - a rebuilt N47D20C engine (£2,500-£3,800) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A C118 CLA 220d is worth £10,000-£25,000 - a rebuilt OM654 engine (£2,800-£4,200) is usually well within the car's value. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the N47D20C and OM654 engines in the CLA 220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N47D20C is a BMW-sourced 2.0-litre diesel used in the C117 CLA 220d (2015-2019), producing 177 hp with a rear-mounted timing chain. The OM654.920 is Mercedes' own 2.0-litre modular diesel used in the C118 CLA 220d (2019-present), producing 190 hp and 400 Nm torque. The N47D20C is notorious for timing chain failure, while the OM654 has injector seal, HPFP, and turbo issues.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz CLA 220d to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the CLA 220d depends on the engine and generation. On N47D20C engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On OM654 engines, turbocharger failure, HPFP failure, or NOx sensor issues are common culprits. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz CLA 220d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The CLA 220d badge has represented the core diesel offering across two generations of the Mercedes-Benz CLA. The first-generation C117 (2013-2019) initially used Mercedes' own OM651 2.1-litre diesel before switching to the BMW-sourced N47D20C 2.0-litre in the 2015 facelift - an engine now notorious for timing chain failures driving UK replacement demand. The second-generation C118 (2019-present) introduced Mercedes' advanced OM654 2.0-litre modular diesel, offering improved efficiency and reduced emissions.

milestones.description: OM651 DE22 LA, 2.1L diesel, 170 hp - C117 CLA 220 CDI launch; 350 Nm torque; rear-mounted timing chain
N47D20C, 2.0L diesel, 177 hp (130 kW) - C117 CLA 220d facelift launch; BMW-sourced engine; 350 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 7.7 seconds
OM654.920, 2.0L diesel, 190 hp (140 kW) - C118 CLA 220d launch; 400 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 7.2 seconds
Model year updates with revised emissions calibration; OM654 continues

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz CLA 220d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The CLA 220d has been powered by two distinct diesel engines across the C117 and C118 generations - the BMW-sourced N47D20C and the Mercedes OM654. The N47D20C is notorious for timing chain tensioner failure, while the OM654 has injector and emissions system issues. Rebuilt CLA 220d engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: N47D20C Timing Chain Failure - Why the C117 CLA 220d Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The N47D20C uses a timing chain positioned at the rear of the engine, adjacent to the flywheel. The chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to slacken and stretch. A metallic rattling or slapping noise from the rear of the engine - particularly at 2,500-3,000 rpm - is the classic warning sign. If the chain snaps, inlet and exhaust valves collide with pistons, causing catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, and sprockets (gearbox removal required)
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt N47D20C with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical C117 CLA 220d is worth £4,000-£8,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £5,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,400-£1,900) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt N47D20C with warranty (£2,500-£3,800) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold starts - especially between 60,000 and 100,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.

problems.group: OM654 Injector Seal Leak & HPFP Failure
problems.h4: OM654 Injector Seal Leak & HPFP Failure - C118 CLA 220d Fuel System Issues
problems.rootCause: The OM654 engine can suffer from injector seal leaks causing oil seepage and "black death" residue around the injectors. High-pressure fuel pump failures are also reported, often related to injector issues or fuel contamination, potentially causing misfires and poor acceleration. Turbocharger failures can cause reduced power, odd noises, and excess exhaust smoke.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, replace seals and bolts
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if injectors are not seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace high-pressure fuel pump, all four injectors, fuel rail
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump has failed and contaminated the system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM654 with upgraded injectors and HPFP
repairOptions.longevity: Required if fuel system contamination has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C118 CLA 220d experiences rough running, misfires, or a diesel smell in the cabin, have the injector seals and HPFP inspected immediately. A £500-£800 seal replacement is significantly cheaper than a £1,800 HPFP replacement or a £2,800 engine replacement. Regular fuel filter changes and using high-quality diesel are essential preventative measures.

problems.h4: OM654 Turbocharger & NOx Sensor Failures - Emissions System Issues
problems.rootCause: The OM654's turbocharger can suffer from premature failure, with symptoms including reduced power, odd noises, and excess exhaust smoke. NOx sensor failures are also common, triggering the check engine light and potentially causing limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace upstream and/or downstream NOx sensors, ECU software update
Complete engine with upgraded turbo and emissions components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C118 CLA 220d experiences reduced power or unusual noises from the engine bay, have the turbocharger and NOx sensors inspected promptly. A £500-£900 turbo repair or £600-£1,200 NOx sensor replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement.

problems.h4: N47D20C EGR Cooler & DPF Issues - Diesel Emission System Failures
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler can develop micro-cracks, causing coolant loss and potential engine overheating. DPF clogging is common on vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, flush cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before engine damage
For DPF blockage; try clean first

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with upgraded EGR and DPF components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if coolant ingestion or DPF failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If you experience low coolant warnings or a loss of power, have the EGR cooler and DPF system inspected promptly. A £500-£900 EGR cooler replacement or £350-£800 DPF clean is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement.
